note: The suite's declared, pre-existing red. `tests/baselines/README.md` states this repository's definition of green: 'no worse than the recorded baseline', never 'all pass'. Continuous integration has to implement that definition or it is red on day one for a failure the plan already owns -- and a permanently-red CI is one everybody learns to ignore. This is the same shrink-only ratchet shape as ceiling-debt.json, modularity-debt.json, test-ownership-debt.json and portability-debt.json, and it bites in BOTH directions: an UNDECLARED failure is a gate failure (a new break cannot hide behind an old one), and a DECLARED failure that starts PASSING is ALSO a gate failure, so a fixed row cannot linger as a standing excuse. There is no flag to skip it. EMPTY IS THE INTENDED END STATE, and this file reached it: plan task 89 fixed the one row it carried (the `multi-tenancy` placeholder-as-a-person false positive) and deleted it, as direction two requires. The gate that proves the two directions runs against a SYNTHETIC row for exactly this reason -- a proof that indexed the live rows would have evaporated on the day the last defect was fixed. Adding a row is legal; it must name the plan task that removes it and state a diagnosis over 80 characters, and it may only ever shrink again.
